drivers: one in-process Python module is the required interface (unified/identity.py)
strong consistency between accounts, identities, sessions and roles
standard library only, no services or infrastructure

alternatives.reason: separate identity and role services would add network calls and distributed data for three small features and break the required in-process interface
sign-in and role checks are synchronous and must be consistent immediately (a role change must apply to the next whoami)
there is no existing system that must stay separate

style.reason: The simplest design that meets every driver: logical modules as classes inside one file with one store

stack.storage: in-memory store owned by the app instance (create_app()), guarded by a lock

reasons.language: Required by the task (standard library only) and the language of all three sources
reasons.storage: Sources keep state in memory; the interface has no persistence; one store per app instance keeps tests isolated
reasons.password_hashing: Keeps A's algorithm (own code) with a stronger default iteration count, recorded per hash so it can be raised
reasons.tests: Built into Python; no install needed

modules.name: config
modules.responsibility: Settings with defaults, overridable per app instance and by environment variables

modules.name: access-control
modules.responsibility: Unified role set, permission table, can(), source role mapping

modules.name: accounts
modules.responsibility: User records, email normalisation and ownership, password hashing, registration, bootstrap admin

modules.name: sessions
modules.responsibility: Password login, token issue, whoami, logout, expiry

modules.name: federation
modules.responsibility: OAuth sign-in: identity lookup, verified-email account linking, account creation

modules.name: role-admin
modules.responsibility: Admin-only role changes with the no-self-raise rule

entities.name: User
entities.notes: One account per person. B's provider and subject move to Identity (not lost).

entities.name: Identity
entities.notes: Federated identities from B: provider and subject (B:Account.provider, B:Account.subject) linked to one User.

auth.method: password (A) and OAuth provider callback (B) into one identity store
auth.session: opaque random bearer token (secrets.token_urlsafe(32)) held server-side with expiry; revoked on logout; an HTTP layer added later should carry it in an http-only, secure cookie

design_system.note: No UI in scope: the deliverable is an in-process Python module

slices.name: Sign in with password or OAuth, whoami, logout
Roles, role mapping and admin role changes

decisions.decision: Modular monolith in one file app/unified/identity.py, logical modules as classes
decisions.reason: Required interface and import path; consistency; no infrastructure

decisions.decision: One User entity with uuid4-hex text ids; Identity (provider, subject) -> User; Session token -> User
OAuth joins an existing account only when email_verified is True; otherwise a separate account; unverified emails never own an address
Roles viewer/editor/admin from C; A user -> editor, B member -> viewer; map_source_role raises KeyError for unknown apps or roles
set_role: caller from token; PermissionError unless admin; role validated; raising your own role refused; invalid token raises an error that is both AuthError and PermissionError
bootstrap_admin works only while no admin exists
decisions.reason: Setup-only step; prevents creating admins later without an admin

decisions.decision: Opaque server-side session tokens with 12-hour expiry and logout
decisions.reason: A had no expiry or revocation (A-E04)

decisions.decision: PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256, 310000 iterations default, per-user salt, constant-time compare, iteration count stored per hash
Duplicate email registration rejected (error is both AuthError and ValueError)
